ranking.note: Moved up: it changes the shape of every blocking Mining IPC call per agreed RFC #33575, so it should land before more consumers build on the interrupt methods.
Moved down: valuable developer tooling and end-to-end coverage, but it sits behind the interface and bug-fix work it exercises.
Lowered to P4: reviewers state the no-mempool case is theoretical in production, making this a narrow interface-contract tidy-up rather than a real bug fix.

inconsistencies: Chain: #36357 is based on #36356; review #36356 first, even though the user-visible getmininginfo fix lives in #36357.

#35581 introduces BlockTemplateManager, which #33922 (reference counting), #36356 (template cache) and #36357 (assembler statics) all build on or extend; #35581 should be settled first to avoid repeated rebasing of the manager's shape.
#35598 was extracted from #33922 and covers the same waitNext/feeThreshold behaviour; if #33922 lands with its own coverage, #35598 becomes redundant.
#36389 deduplicates the validation-state catcher that #35581 and #36356 move into BlockTemplateManager; it should be reviewed after those land or it will churn.

#35300 (precious on submitBlock/submitSolution) and #36097 (cancellation arguments) both change Mining capnp ordinals and will collide; sequence them deliberately, with #36097 first since it sets the interface convention.
result.notes: The category splits cleanly: three P2s that extend or make efficient the interface external (Stratum v2) miners build on, a broad P3 middle of real but bounded fixes, tooling and tests, and two P4s that are internal or theoretical. No PR here carries a template-validity or fund-loss consequence, so nothing reaches P1.
